newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court charges Kurd guards with extortion.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court charges Kurd guards with extortion.

text.p: A Turkish court has charged two members of an anti-rebel Kurdish militia with extorting money from villagers under the pretext of being separatist guerrillas, local officials said on Wednesday.

Officials at the governor's office in the southeastern town of Batman said the suspects, two brothers, were arrested on Tuesday. They had told villagers they were collecting money for the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebel group.

Around 70,000 village guards, mostly Kurds, are enrolled to help government troops in the fight against the PKK. Doubts have been cast on the future of the militia recently because of the alleged involvement in serious crimes by some of its members.
More than 21,000 people have died in the 12-year-old conflict between troops and the PKK, fighting for autonomy or independence in the southeast.
